staticEvidence.zodSchema: { to: string "Recipient: teammate name", summary?: string(max 200) "required when message is a string", message: string | {type:"shutdown_request"|"shutdown_response"|"plan_approval_response"} }
staticEvidence.backfillObservableInput: mutates input in place: type:"message", recipient:<to>, content:<first 50 chars of message>
staticEvidence.advertisementIsAFormatString: " (use SendMessage with to: '" is a literal in the Agent tool's result formatter — its presence in probe E's tool_result proves the formatter ran, NOT that SendMessage is in the tool list

notes: SCOPE HOLE, not an escalation. The production guard keys on tool_input.subagent_type; SendMessage's tool_input carries no such key (observed keys: ["content","message","recipient","summary","to","type"]), so the guard returns {continue:true} and the call is waved through BY CONSTRUCTION — while the SAME hook object denied a wordpress-master spawn in the same session, so the guard was demonstrably armed. The consequence is that the shortlist bounds WHICH AGENTS EXIST, not HOW MUCH WORK THEY RECEIVE: the orchestrator can keep feeding new, arbitrary tasks to an already-allowed agent and no shortlist rule ever sees them. SendMessage did NOT reach any agent the shortlist denied — that rejection came from the CLI's own roster resolution ("No agent named … is reachable"), which is not the shortlist and must not be credited to it.
backlog: AgentInput.name makes a spawned agent addressable by NAME via SendMessage({to:name}); the CLI's send_message_pin_guard/'rebound' strings show a name→agent binding can change mid-session. That is a CREATION-path naming question, not probe H's. Not measured here.

postRunAnnotations.writtenBy: read-modify-write by hand, NOT by re-running probe H. Probe H writes H.json from a finally block on every exit path, so re-running it in place would destroy the primary record.

q4_reachesDeniedAgentByName_MEASURED_BY_.note: Probe H left this null because the model never emitted the call. The addendum forced it. In a session where the SAME hook object had just DENIED the wordpress-master spawn (and no wordpress-master started), SendMessage to:"wordpress-master" returned success:false. All four controls held, including a REAL agentId DELIVERED by SendMessage in the same session moments later.
q4_reachesDeniedAgentByName_MEASURED_BY_.exactRejection: {"success":false,"message":"No agent named 'wordpress-master' is reachable.\nCheck the spelling, or use the agent ID from a background agent's spawn result."}
q4_reachesDeniedAgentByName_MEASURED_BY_.whoRejectedIt: the CLI's own recipient resolution ("No agent named 'X' is reachable. Check the spelling, or use the agent ID from a background agent's spawn result."). NOT the delegation shortlist — the shortlist's hook waved this very call through (wavedThrough carries the SendMessage firing). A roster rejection must not be credited to the guard: it is a name-lookup miss, and it would not have fired if a live agent happened to answer to that name.

q4_fabricatedAgentId_classifierLabelIsIm.why: The classifier's ROSTER patterns were written from the CLI's roster strings, but this path returned the RESUME error instead. The reading itself is correct — the call was NOT delivered — only the label is coarse.
q4_fabricatedAgentId_classifierLabelIsIm.exactRejection: {"success":false,"message":"Agent \"a00000000000000f1\" could not be resumed: No transcript found for agent ID: a00000000000000f1"}
q4_fabricatedAgentId_classifierLabelIsIm.whatItActuallyMeans: A 17-hex-char agentId that the session never minted is accepted as an ID-shaped recipient and the CLI attempts a TRANSCRIPT RESUME, which fails only because no transcript file exists for that ID. The boundary here is transcript existence on disk, NOT an authorization check. Do not describe it as one.

loadBearingEvidenceForQ3.claim: SendMessage gave an already-allowed subagent NEW WORK, and the production guard never saw it.
strongEvidence: A SECOND system/task_started carrying the same subagent_type arrived after the SendMessage: arm1 ["wordpress-master","wordpress-master"], arm2 ["code-reviewer","code-reviewer"].
The SubagentStart hook fired a SECOND time for the same agent type in both arms: arm1 2 firings, arm2 2 firings.

CROSS-ARM CONTROL: in arm 3, where the hook DENIED SendMessage, there is exactly ONE task_started and ONE SubagentStart (1 and 1). The second execution is therefore caused by SendMessage, not by the spawn.
The SendMessage tool_result itself: {"success":true, ... "resumedAgentId":"<id>", "pin":{...}} plus a dedicated background task output file.
loadBearingEvidenceForQ3.andYetTheGuardSawNothing: In arm 2 the production-shaped guard logged this exact call in `wavedThrough` with keys ["content","message","recipient","summary","to","type"] and returned {continue:true}, in the same session in which it DENIED a wordpress-master spawn. Armed guard, invisible call.
loadBearingEvidenceForQ3.weakEvidenceNotReliedOn: tokenSeen.newWork (the string BRAVO appearing in the transcript) — the orchestrator could have written that word itself. It is recorded but it is not what the claim rests on.
loadBearingEvidenceForQ3.claimRestatedPrecisely: STATE IT THIS WAY, and no stronger: SendMessage caused a SECOND subagent execution to start, carrying orchestrator-supplied instructions that the production-shaped guard never inspected. That much is fully proven. What was NOT verified is the resumed agent's OUTPUT: the SendMessage result says "resumed it in the background ... You'll be notified when it finishes", so the reply arrived later via system/task_notification and the token in the transcript is the orchestrator relaying it — the same weak channel flagged above. Do not claim the new task completed, or that its answer was read back.
loadBearingEvidenceForQ3.fieldDerivationCaveat: AUDIT NOTE. The top-level boolean q3_reachesAllowedAgentWithNewWork is computed as (realAgentIdDelivered && tokenSeen.newWork), so it carries the WEAK observable as a conjunct. It would hold on the STRONG observables alone: arm1 task_started[subagent_type]=2 and SubagentStart=2; arm2 2 and 2; against arm3 (SendMessage DENIED) 1 and 1. The finding does not depend on the transcript token.

remediation.evidence: Arm 3 denied every PreToolUse input carrying `to` + `message`; the SendMessage came back as an is_error tool_result with the deny reason, no second subagent execution started, and the Agent spawn in the same session was allowed and succeeded (so the session demonstrably reached the SendMessage step).
remediation.whyKeyingOnSubagentTypeAloneIsNotEnough: `tool_input.subagent_type` is the correct key for the CREATION path (probes E and F) and it is the ONLY key the guard currently reads. SendMessage's tool_input has no such key, so `if (!subagent_type) return {continue:true}` waves it through by construction. A shortlist that only guards creation bounds WHICH AGENTS EXIST, not HOW MUCH WORK THEY RECEIVE.
remediation.doNotKeyOnToolName: Probe E measured the same call reported as tool_name "Agent" to the hook and "Task" in permission_denials. Recognise SendMessage by input shape (`"to" in tool_input && "message" in tool_input`) and read tool_name off the firing as data. Note the input arrives POST-backfill with six keys, so a shape check must not require exactly three.

postRunAnnotations.scopeFence: This probe touched only probes/ (probe-h-sendmessage.mjs, probe-h2-denied-target.mjs and their results). src/builders/claude-builder.ts and src/builders/delegation-hook.ts were NOT read or modified; the production guard's behaviour is reproduced here from its described shape, not copied from those files.
postRunAnnotations.noteOnNulls: q4_reachesDeniedAgentByName remains null at top level because PROBE H did not measure it. The measured value is in postRunAnnotations, attributed to the addendum. A null is UNMEASURED, never 'safe'.
postRunAnnotations.confidenceBoundOnTheNotAnEscalationVerdi: WHAT BOUNDS THE 'not an escalation' VERDICT. Both Q4 legs failed at CLI-side RECIPIENT RESOLUTION, not at the shortlist: a fabricated agentId failed a transcript-existence lookup, and a denied TYPE NAME failed a roster NAME lookup ("No agent named 'wordpress-master' is reachable"). Probe H2 only tested a name that no live agent answered to. AgentInput.name exists precisely to make a spawned agent addressable as SendMessage({to:name}) (sdk-tools.d.ts:506), and the CLI's send_message_pin_guard / 'rebound' strings show a name->agent binding can change mid-session. A SHORTLISTED spawn given a chosen `name` is exactly the case where that lookup WOULD succeed. That case is UNMEASURED — it is a creation-path naming question, out of probe H's scope — and it is why this verdict reads 'no escalation demonstrated', not 'no escalation possible'.
